questions.q: Which two abilities does emotional intelligence rest on?
a: Emotional self-awareness and self-regulation
Verbal fluency and mathematical reasoning
Optimism and physical resilience
Empathy and public speaking skill
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the two parts of emotional intelligence are emotional self-awareness and emotional self-regulation.

a: Recognizing and labeling what you are feeling
Hiding your feelings from other people
Feeling emotions more intensely than others
Explaining your feelings to anyone who asks
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines self-awareness as being able to recognize and name your feelings, as children learn to do with anger.

questions.q: What did Goleman find about students with more empathy?
a: They earned better grades than equally smart peers
They preferred socializing to studying
They were less likely to finish their degrees
They scored lower on standard intelligence tests
questions.why: Lesson 2 says students with higher empathy get better grades even when their peers are just as smart.

questions.q: How does mirroring someone's body language help you?
a: It builds rapport and makes you more empathic
It tricks them into agreeing with your opinions
It helps you hide your true emotional state
It makes you appear more dominant in a group
questions.why: Lesson 3 says mirroring sends trust cues, shows you how the other person feels and builds empathy.

questions.q: How does an optimist explain a failure?
a: As temporary, external and something they can change
As permanent, personal and impossible to avoid
As proof that the task was never worth doing
As a result of other people's bad decisions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says optimists see bad events as temporary, external and specific, and believe they can improve next time.
